change_checks.reason: The bounds f(x)>-0.385 and y>0.990 give a crossing time below 0.5/0.605<0.827. For k≥100, total input is at most 0.01, yielding -1≤x≤-0.49; the subsequent trapping argument proves convergence to -1. The stated rate ranges are sufficient, not an asserted exact threshold.

change_checks.reason: The equation for x-z is correct and establishes comparison. The upper bound then proves convergence to 1 for x>0 and y≥0. The time-shift argument preserves the distinction between crossing x=0 and crossing a basin boundary.

change_checks.location: Choosing a withdrawal that works; Appendix A.4
change_checks.what_changed: The successful release procedure and absence of a uniform settling deadline are summarized in the main text.
change_checks.reason: The bound c=1-2/(3√3)>0.615 gives a zero-reaching time below 0.814, so x is positive at time one for every k>0. After release, the necessary condition t≥log(1/δ)/k excludes a common finite deadline for any fixed 0<δ<1.

change_checks.reason: For each fixed finite T≥0, rates 0<k≤0.01/(T+1) retain sufficient positive input, while k≥100 gives remaining input e^(-kT)/k≤0.01. Thus both endpoints remain possible for every such fixed wait.
